headline: Google may use your Gmail and Photos data for ads if you opt-in to AI features
summary: The updated privacy policy, effective October 16th, allows data from these services to be used for personalized ads if connected to AI features like Personal Intelligence. This changes a previous promise not to use this data for ads.
details: Google has updated its privacy policy to allow targeted ads based on personal data, specifically if users opt into personalized AI features. This change, effective October 16th, adds an exception to its previous promise regarding Gmail, Drive, and Google Photos.

The policy now states that data can be used "unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads." This applies to users who connect these services to AI Mode and other Search tools via Google's Personal Intelligence feature.

The intention is to provide more personalized AI responses and recommendations by leveraging a deeper understanding of user data. Consequently, users who enable these features may now see ads targeted based on the content within their Drive, Gmail, or Photos.

Google clarifies that advertisers will not gain direct access to users' Drive, Gmail, or Photos information, nor personally identifying details like names or email addresses. The company also assures that ads will not be shown based on sensitive categories such as race, sexual orientation, religion, or health.

Users retain control over their data and can prevent personal information from being used for targeted ads. Options include disconnecting specific apps from Search's Personal Intelligence features or disabling Personalized Recommendations entirely via the Search Services Personalization settings page.

headline: The iPhone Duo gets 7/10 in Verge review, sparking debate over its design
summary: The Vergecast debated the 7/10 score, with some suggesting the outer screen might be 'the worst iPhone ever' and that the device might have been better conceived as an iPad.
details: The Verge gave the new iPhone Duo a score of 7 out of 10, acknowledging the significant challenge of reviewing and assessing such a novel concept for the most popular smartphone in history.

On The Vergecast, hosts David and Nilay debated the score, considering if the outer screen, as suggested by John Gruber, could be 'the worst iPhone ever.' They also explored whether the product would have been better received if it had launched as an iPad Duo.

The discussion highlighted the potential for the Duo to improve over time, but questioned its viability as a phone for everyone. The podcast also touched on other topics, including a major PHP cybersecurity flaw, the impact of AI shopping on retailers, and confusing Gemini news.
